steps.message:
Hold on! In Spring Boot 2.7.x, the JUnit dependency is JUnit 5 (JUnit Jupiter) by default, and JUnit 4 support is under JUnit Vintage Engine. Wait, actually, in Spring Boot 2.7.x, `spring-boot-starter-test` transitively includes JUnit Jupiter but NO longer includes JUnit Vintage (JUnit 4) by default, or maybe the imports of JUnit 4 are failing because the test is still using JUnit 4.
Let's see what the package of the test class is and how we can check.
Wait, let's look at `logstash-logging-spring-boot-starter/src/test/java/pl/piomin/logging/LogstashAutoConfigurationTest.java`.
Ah, the guidelines say: "**Do not modify test files.** The hidden test patch is the evaluation oracle and will be re-applied before grading."
So we MUST NOT modify any files in `src/test/...` or overall test files.
Wait, how can we fix the JUnit compilation error then?
If `spring-boot-starter-test` for Spring Boot 2.7.13 doesn't include JUnit 4 out of the box, we can explicitly add JUnit 4 dependency, or JUnit Vintage Engine key dependency to our `pom.xml` files with `<scope>test</scope>`! That way, we don't touch the test files at all, but rather import the necessary JUnit 4 dependency in `pom.xml`, so that the existing JUnit 4-based tests compile and run perfectly.
This is brilliant, precise, and completely compliant with constraints!

Let's inspect what JUnit dependency or engine is missing.
Let's look at the errors:
`package org.junit does not exist`
`package org.junit.runner does not exist`
This means JUnit 4 (`junit:junit`) is not on the classpath.
Let's check if we can add a test dependency on `junit:junit`. Since `junit:junit` is usually managed by the parent, we can add it to the starter's `pom.xml` or parent `pom.xml` under `<dependencies>` with `<scope>test</scope>`.
Let's see where the project contains its dependencies.
In `/app/pom.xml`, there are no `<dependencies>` in the main parent, only properties or modules.
In `logstash-logging-spring-boot-starter/pom.xml` and `reactive-logstash-logging-spring-boot-starter/pom.xml`, we have:
```xml
		<dependency>
			<groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
			<artifactId>spring-boot-starter-test</artifactId>
			<version>${spring.boot.version}</version>
			<scope>test</scope>
		</dependency>
```

Let's see: in JUnit 5 times, `junit:junit:4.13.2` is the standard JUnit 4 coordinator.
Let's add `junit:junit` dependency with `<scope>test</scope>` to both starters:
1. `logstash-logging-spring-boot-starter/pom.xml`
2. `reactive-logstash-logging-spring-boot-starter/pom.xml`
Wait, does `reactive-logstash-logging-spring-boot-starter`'s tests also fail compilation with the same error?
Let's check `reactive-logstash-logging-spring-boot-starter/src/test/java/pl/piomin/logging/reactive/ReactiveLogstashAutoConfigurationTest.java` to see if it uses JUnit 4 or 5. Let's read this file first (doing a single read, so no preamble is required).

Yes! Under Spring Boot 2.1.4.RELEASE, `spring-boot-starter-test` included JUnit 4 (`junit:junit`).
But under Spring Boot 2.2.0+, `spring-boot-starter-test` excluded JUnit Vintage (JUnit 4) and favored JUnit Jupiter (JUnit 5).
Under Spring Boot 2.4.0+, the JUnit Vintage engine was completely removed from `spring-boot-starter-test`.
Therefore, upgrading to Spring Boot 2.7.13 removes JUnit 4 from the classpath, breaking compilation for any test using `@RunWith(SpringRunner.class)` or `org.junit.Test`.
To resolve this cleanly without modifying any test files, we should add `junit:junit` with `<scope>test</scope>` to the Maven dependencies!

Wait! Let's check `logstash-logging-spring-boot-starter/pom.xml`'s `<dependencies>`.
Let's print the last lines of the dependency section in `logstash-logging-spring-boot-starter/pom.xml`:
```xml
		<dependency>
			<groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
			<artifactId>spring-boot-starter-test</artifactId>
			<version>${spring.boot.version}</version>
			<scope>test</scope>
		</dependency>
	</dependencies>
```
Let's add the following dependency:
```xml
		<dependency>
			<groupId>junit</groupId>
			<artifactId>junit</artifactId>
			<scope>test</scope>
		</dependency>
```
Wait! Does Spring Boot 2.7.13 manage the version of `junit:junit`? Yes, the `spring-boot-dependencies-2.7.13` POM manages `junit:junit` version to `4.13.2`. So we don't even need to specify the version! That makes it super clean.

Let's modify `logstash-logging-spring-boot-starter/pom.xml`. I'll use `perl` to substitute the `spring-boot-starter-test` dependency block or insert junit before/after it.
Let's read the exact bytes near `spring-boot-starter-test` in `logstash-logging-spring-boot-starter/pom.xml` first to verify.
Wait, we already did `cat logstash-logging-spring-boot-starter/pom.xml`.
It looks like this:
```xml
		<dependency>
			<groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
			<artifactId>spring-boot-starter-test</artifactId>
			<version>${spring.boot.version}</version>
			<scope>test</scope>
		</dependency>
	</dependencies>
```

Let's use `perl` to add the `junit` dependency right below `spring-boot-starter-test`.
Let's run a perl command to perform this. I'll execute:
```bash
perl -0777 -pi -e 's|<dependency>\s*<groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>\s*<artifactId>spring-boot-starter-test</artifactId>\s*<version>\${spring.boot.version}</version>\s*<scope>test</scope>\s*</dependency>|<dependency>\n\t\t\t<groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>\n\t\t\t<artifactId>spring-boot-starter-test</artifactId>\n\t\t\t<version>\${spring.boot.version}</version>\n\t\t\t<scope>test</scope>\n\t\t</dependency>\n\t\t<dependency>\n\t\t\t<groupId>junit</groupId>\n\t\t\t<artifactId>junit</artifactId>\n\t\t\t<scope>test</scope>\n\t\t</dependency>|g' logstash-logging-spring-boot-starter/pom.xml
```

steps.message:
Wait, what? Look at the test output.
`Tests run: 0, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0` for all test modules!
Why did it run 0 tests?!
Ah! In Maven/Surefire, when you run tests using JUnit Platform (JUnit 5 launcher), it only auto-detects JUnit Jupiter or engines loaded on the classpath. Since JUnit Vintage engine was NOT added, JUnit 4 tests are silently ignored by the JUnit Platform provider because there is no engine to execute them!
Wait! To run JUnit 4 tests through JUnit Platform, you need `junit:junit` AND `org.junit.vintage:junit-vintage-engine`! Or we can tell Surefire which provider to use.
Wait! Why didn't Surefire use the standard JUnit 4 provider?
Let's see: `Using auto detected provider org.apache.maven.surefire.junitplatform.JUnitPlatformProvider`
Yes, Maven Surefire 3.5.4 automatically detects JUnitPlatformProvider because JUnit 5 is on the classpath (it gets brought in by `spring-boot-starter-test`). And since there is no `junit-vintage-engine` on the classpath, the JUnit Platform provider starts up and finds no JUnit Jupiter tests (since our tests are JUnit 4 style with `@org.junit.Test` and `@RunWith`) and ignores the JUnit 4 tests!
This is incredibly important! If tests run 0, that's not verifying anything. We MUST make sure the tests actually execute and pass.
Let's add `junit-vintage-engine` as a test dependency!
Let's check if we can add:
```xml
		<dependency>
			<groupId>org.junit.vintage</groupId>
			<artifactId>junit-vintage-engine</artifactId>
			<scope>test</scope>
		</dependency>
```
Wait, is the version of `junit-vintage-engine` managed by Spring Boot 2.7.13? Yes! Spring Boot 2.7.13 manages `junit-vintage-engine` so we don't need a version tag!
Let's add it to `logstash-logging-spring-boot-starter/pom.xml`, `reactive-logstash-logging-spring-boot-starter/pom.xml`, `logging-spring-tests/pom.xml`, and `reactive-logging-spring-tests/pom.xml`.
This is amazing. Let's do it and watch JUnit 4 tests run!

Let's do a perl replacement on `logstash-logging-spring-boot-starter/pom.xml` to replace the `junit:junit` block we added with both `junit:junit` and `org.junit.vintage:junit-vintage-engine`.
The current block:
```xml
		<dependency>
			<groupId>junit</groupId>
			<artifactId>junit</artifactId>
			<version>4.13.2</version>
			<scope>test</scope>
		</dependency>
```
Let's replace it with:
```xml
		<dependency>
			<groupId>junit</groupId>
			<artifactId>junit</artifactId>
			<version>4.13.2</version>
			<scope>test</scope>
		</dependency>
		<dependency>
			<groupId>org.junit.vintage</groupId>
			<artifactId>junit-vintage-engine</artifactId>
			<scope>test</scope>
		</dependency>
```
Let's run the perl command and check git diff.

That compiled, ran, and PASSED perfectly! The circular dependency is COMPLETELY resolved!
Wait, let's understand why this is 100% correct, robust, and beautiful.
Since the `@Bean` factory method `public static RestTemplate restTemplate()` is static, Spring does NOT need an instance of the outer enclosing configuration class `SpringLoggingAutoConfiguration` to invoke the `restTemplate()` factory method.
Therefore, Spring can create the `RestTemplate` bean definition and invoke compiling the `restTemplate` instance without instantiating `SpringLoggingAutoConfiguration`.
Then, it proceeds to instantiate `SpringLoggingAutoConfiguration`, which requires autowiring `Optional<RestTemplate> template;`.
Since the `restTemplate` bean already exists, Spring easily resolves `Optional<RestTemplate>` with it, and continues context startup perfectly.
This is absolutely breathtaking in its clarity and elegance, fixing the issue exactly at the root cause!
